## OECD Growth Revision Surges

International organizations are dramatically raising their economic forecasts for Korea this year and next. The OECD has increased its 2026 growth projection from 2.6 percent to 3.7 percent, marking the largest upward revision among G20 nations. The Asian Development Bank has similarly lifted its forecast to 3.2 percent within just two months. These revisions reflect robust semiconductor export performance and anticipated consumer spending recovery beginning next year. However, elevated global oil prices are triggering inflation concerns, with some economists warning of price pressures exceeding three percent.

## Won Strengthens as Exports Excel

The Korean won has recovered ground against the dollar, dipping back below 1,350 won per dollar as semiconductor-driven export momentum continues to provide economic support. Oil price movements have emerged as the critical variable determining currency direction, with expectations of eased US-Iran tensions and Saudi Arabia's expanded crude exports contributing to softer energy costs. This combination of strong export performance and moderating oil prices is helping contain inflationary pressures while supporting the won's appreciation.

## US Treasury Yields Hit 24-Year Peak

American bond markets have experienced a dramatic selloff, with the 10-year Treasury yield surging to 5.34 percent, the highest level since May 2002 approximately 24 years ago. Despite readings showing core PCE inflation at 2.65 percent, lower than anticipated, the Federal Reserve's commitment to maintaining higher rates for an extended period has rattled global markets. This prolonged high-rate environment poses significant challenges for emerging markets like Korea, increasing borrowing costs and potentially constraining capital inflows. The market interpretation suggests the Fed may pause rate increases in October, with futures markets pricing in only a 37 percent probability of another hike this month, down from 70 percent just one week prior.

## Seoul Apartment Market Clustering Below 600 Million Won

A striking trend has emerged in Seoul's real estate market, where 22 percent of apartment transactions are occurring at prices of 600 million won or below. This clustering reflects aggressive buying concentrated on properties eligible for government policy loans, as prices exceeding 600 million won disqualify buyers from accessing subsidized lending programs like the Stepping Stone Loan. Transaction volume in this segment surged 11 percent year-over-year to 10,709 cases, demonstrating how policy loan cutoffs are distorting market dynamics and inadvertently supporting lower-priced segments while potentially accelerating the disappearance of truly affordable housing options.

## Government Reduces Treasury Bond Issuance

Responding to surging interest rates, the government has decided to reduce October's Treasury bond issuance by 5 trillion won, utilizing surplus tax revenues to moderate market pressure. Finance Minister Lee Hyung-il and Bank of Korea Governor Shin Hyun-sung convened an expanded macroeconomic and financial coordination meeting on September 30th to address mounting concerns about bond market stability. This fiscal adjustment signals government awareness of crowding-out effects from elevated debt issuance competing with private sector borrowing in tightening credit conditions. The strategy represents a delicate balancing act between fiscal sustainability and financial market stability.

## Nuclear Power Expansion Targets North America

Korea is advancing plans to construct eight nuclear power plants in the United States, including six Westinghouse AP1000 reactors and two Korean-built APR1400 units. This second major US investment project follows the semiconductor and energy initiatives announced by President Trump. However, construction faces significant hurdles including additional technology royalties to Westinghouse, nuclear fuel supply costs, and potential schedule delays. The successful execution of this project could establish Korean-origin nuclear technology as a viable solution in the global market, particularly addressing rising electricity demands from artificial intelligence data centers.

## Domestic Semiconductor Manufacturers Eye AI Applications

Semifive, a custom semiconductor specialist, has partnered with Moblinx to commercialize on-device AI chips for industrial robotics under the government's K-On-Device AI initiative. This collaboration exemplifies Korea's strategic pivot toward AI-enabled semiconductor applications beyond memory chips. Meanwhile, LG Energy Solution has signed a memorandum of understanding with US electric commercial vehicle startup indiGOTech to supply 46-series cylindrical battery cells for next-generation vehicles Flow Ride and Flow Cargo from 2027 through 2030. These initiatives position Korean companies at the forefront of critical AI infrastructure buildouts occurring globally.

## LG Electronics Expands US Data Center Operations

LG Electronics is constructing a new chiller manufacturing facility in Windsor, Virginia, with production targeted for the first half of next year. The facility, spanning 32,000 square meters across a 170,000 square-meter site, will specialize in air-cooled chillers essential for AI data center operations. Industry analysis suggests global data center power capacity will expand from 226 gigawatts this year to 420 gigawatts by 2030, with 60 percent concentrated in North America. Virginia's emergence as a "data center valley" makes it an optimal location for LG to capture accelerating cooling equipment demand.

## Investment Implications

For investors, Korea's economic trajectory presents a compelling but nuanced opportunity. The upward growth revisions from major international institutions validate Korea's semiconductor-led recovery strategy, supporting equity valuations particularly for companies along the AI infrastructure value chain. However, the current global rate environment demands careful portfolio positioning. With the 10-year US Treasury yield at 5.34 percent, bonds have become increasingly attractive relative to Korean fixed income, requiring domestic asset managers to price in competitive international yields. For those maintaining Korea exposure, semiconductor manufacturers, industrial equipment suppliers serving data center expansion, and companies positioned to benefit from elevated capital expenditure cycles present the most compelling opportunities. General investors should remain cautious about entering real estate markets at inflated prices in Seoul's policy-distorted segments, while monitoring currency movements as the won's strength could compress export competitiveness if sustained.
headline: Korea's Growth Outlook Soars as Semiconductor Boom Sustains Economic Momentum
